title: Warming evenness intervals crossed zero in four Cedar Creek planting-group and period tests in 2017-2022
abstract: We tested whether biomass evenness offsets recorded richness loss under warming. We used 432 paired harvest records from two planting groups and two periods at Cedar Creek in 2017-2022. Four adjusted t intervals for log evenness included zero. In later 16-species plots, the mean log evenness contrast was +0.1030 and offset a log richness contrast of -0.0883. A sign-flip reference test gave a Holm p value of 0.0313 for that evenness contrast, so the references differ. A synthetic example showed that missing one species with 0.78 percent of biomass can produce the same evenness increase without a true community change. It does not fit the full observed data. One site, repeated plots, small moving harvest strips and no detection estimates limit inference. We do not establish biological compensation, a repeated regional response or an air pollution effect. Code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: Paired log contrasts for richness, evenness and effective diversity. Intervals use the four-test t cutoff; component diagnostics are not jointly adjusted across all plotted estimates.

citations.reason: Prior paired richness question and sample scope motivate a new diversity decomposition. Source observations overlap fully; no code is reused.
Prior temporal diversity variation study shares the source data but does not test this evenness offset.
